title: Auth config parity: env var discovery, header normalization, and secure redaction
author: Dana Lo
description: Motivation: The TS SDK currently differs from Python/Go in how it discovers API keys and how it constructs auth headers, which is creating support load (SUP-9355) and Security review churn. This PR aligns TypeScript with the cross-SDK auth standard (ENG-2484) by standardizing env var names + precedence, normalizing headers consistently across fetch/undici, and ensuring we never leak secrets in logs/errors. What changed: (1) API key discovery order is now: constructor option `apiKey` (highest priority), then `process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY`, then `process.env.REDWOOD_INFERENCE_API_KEY` (back-compat alias). We intentionally do not read API keys from local files in the TS SDK (Security guidance). (2) Header normalization: the SDK always sends `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; if the caller provided `Authorization` (any casing) we respect it unless they also pass `apiKey` (in which case `apiKey` wins to reduce ambiguity). We also normalize `User-Agent` / `X-Redwood-SDK` and ensure request IDs and other headers preserve caller-provided values without duplicating keys due to casing differences. (3) Error messages: missing/empty key errors are now actionable and consistent: "Missing Redwood API key. Set REDWOOD_API_KEY or pass { apiKey } when constructing the client." Invalid key errors no longer echo header values and do not include any portion of the key. (4) Redaction: we added a `redactHeadersForLog()` utility used by the internal debug logger and error wrapping. It redacts `authorization`, `x-api-key`, `cookie`, and `set-cookie` (case-insensitive) and avoids accidentally stringifying Headers objects with secrets. (5) Tests: unit tests cover env var precedence, header casing behavior, and redaction invariants. Notes: This PR is intentionally scoped to auth config/header behavior and logging redaction (no retry/timeout changes here). Follow-ups: conformance harness will validate auth behavior across SDKs (ENG-2485).
commits: sdk(auth): align apiKey env var discovery with cross-SDK spec
sdk(auth): add header normalization + casing-safe merge
sdk(security): redact sensitive headers in debug logs and error context
test(auth): add env precedence + header normalization regression tests
docs(internal): update auth error message snapshots
notable_snippet: Before: we accepted `process.env.REDWOOD_TOKEN` and set `x-api-key` in some codepaths; we also logged request headers in debug mode without consistent redaction. After: `resolveApiKey()` only checks `REDWOOD_API_KEY` (primary) and `REDWOOD_INFERENCE_API_KEY` (alias), and `buildHeaders()` always produces an `Authorization: Bearer ...` header unless the caller already set Authorization explicitly. `redactHeadersForLog()` replaces secret values with "<redacted>" and is applied before any debug log line is emitted.
review_conversation: Marcus Lin (Security): "Please confirm we do not support reading keys from disk (common exfiltration vector) and that we redact Authorization regardless of header casing." Dana Lo: "Confirmed; TS SDK only reads from constructor options and env vars. Redaction is case-insensitive and covers Authorization/x-api-key/cookies." Kevin Osei (Security): "Error message should not include partial keys (even last 4) and should point to the env var name we want customers to use." Dana Lo: "Updated errors to be remediation-only and standardized on REDWOOD_API_KEY as the primary." Ibrahim Khan (TL): "Precedence between caller-provided Authorization vs apiKey option needs to be explicit; spec says explicit config wins." Dana Lo: "Implemented: if apiKey is provided we overwrite Authorization; otherwise we preserve caller Authorization. Added tests." Elliot Price (Docs): "Can we keep the old env var for one release to avoid breaking existing installs?" Dana Lo: "Kept REDWOOD_INFERENCE_API_KEY as alias; did not keep REDWOOD_TOKEN." Marcus Lin: "Ship it once the redaction helper is used in both debug logger and error wrapper." Dana Lo: "Done; both callsites updated."
release_notes: TypeScript SDK auth is now standardized: use REDWOOD_API_KEY (or client { apiKey }). Authorization header is normalized to Bearer and sensitive headers are always redacted in debug logs/errors. Back-compat: REDWOOD_INFERENCE_API_KEY is still accepted as an alias for this release.
